entities.summary:
Bayer AG, founded 1863 in Barmen, Germany by Friedrich Bayer and Johann Friedrich Weskott as a synthetic dye manufacturer, is one of the world's largest pharmaceutical and agricultural science companies — known for aspirin (Bayer's most iconic product, first synthesized by Felix Hoffmann at Bayer in 1897), heroin (also first synthesized by Bayer in 1898 and marketed as a cough suppressant until 1913), and glyphosate (Roundup herbicide, inherited through the $63 billion acquisition of Monsanto in 2018). Bayer's history encapsulates both the triumphs and controversies of 20th-century German science.

Bayer chemist Felix Hoffmann synthesized acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) on August 10, 1897, producing a stable form of a compound known for centuries in willow bark. Aspirin became the world's best-selling drug for most of the 20th century — over 40,000 tonnes consumed annually worldwide. In the same period, Hoffmann synthesized diacetylmorphine (heroin) — Bayer trademarked the name 'Heroin' and marketed it as a non-addictive cough suppressant 1898-1913, sold over the counter in 23 countries.

Bayer was part of I.G. Farben (1925-1945) — the industrial conglomerate that manufactured Zyklon B for the Nazi Holocaust and used concentration camp labor. Bayer was reconstituted as an independent company after WWII. The 2018 Monsanto acquisition — including glyphosate's Roundup — immediately embroiled Bayer in massive litigation: US courts have awarded billions in damages to cancer patients claiming glyphosate caused their non-Hodgkin lymphoma, with Bayer settling for $10+ billion.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bayer's simultaneous invention of aspirin (the 20th century's most beneficial drug) and heroin (one of its most destructive) on the same day in 1897 — by the same chemist — is history's most striking illustration that the same chemical ingenuity can produce salvation and catastrophe simultaneously.
